solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leader with due deference to me

parts.note: pace is a Latin preposition used in English to mean 'with due respect to' someone you disagree with
in crosswords 'me' often stands for the setter who wrote the clue

explanation.surface: Someone addresses a leader with respectful deference, as if bowing to the speaker's own authority.
explanation.walkthrough: PACE, used before a name when politely disagreeing, is an English borrowing from Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter sets the speed others follow, so is the one in front: a leader in a race or a trend.

clue.text: Hostelry I call chaotic with rules for everyone

parts.note: a pub is a hostelry, an inn

indicators.note: chaotic means in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: At a pub, someone calls things chaotic and demands rules for all the customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaotic' rearranges I CALL to LICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Public law governs the state and its relations with the public, so it applies to all citizens.

clue.text: Start to chase a red squirrel away

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Che Guevara was a famous red, a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Something sets off chasing a red squirrel off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red squirrel' looks like the animal; 'red' is Che, and 'squirrel away' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cache is to hide something away for later, as a squirrel hoards nuts.

clue.text: Bill's extra procedure in court accusation

parts.note: a service is how a point begins on a tennis court
a charge is a formal accusation

explanation.surface: A lawyer's bill includes an extra for a court procedure on a criminal accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' is a tennis court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A service charge is an extra percentage added to a restaurant bill for the staff.

clue.text: Monkey stopping to beat one set of drums

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so this piece goes inside another

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a little monkey is a mischievous child, an imp
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A monkey stops to bang on a drum kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' is an imp, not an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums, played as a set in the orchestra.

clue.text: Heard on EastEnders, very cultural feature

indicators.note: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in East London, where the Cockney accent drops the H, so the word is said that way

parts.note: highbrow means intellectual, very cultured

explanation.surface: A remark on the TV soap that it is very cultural.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running British TV soap opera in a Cockney setting; dropping the H turns 'highbrow' into ''ighbrow'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebrow is one of the features of the face.

clue.text: In Celsius, one divides hot and cold

indicators.note: a piece that divides two others sits between them, so one letter goes in the middle of the other pair

parts.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot
C is the tap abbreviation for cold
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A little physics: on the Celsius scale, the one degree point splits hot from cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to Celsius, but it is the definition, in its sense of fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In' as an adjective means fashionable or stylish, which is what chic means.

clue.text: Not half hard-up, money's in cash one's blown

indicators.note: not half suggests taking only half, here the first half of each word

explanation.surface: Someone hard up is stuffing money into their cash box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' takes the front halves: HAR, MON, I, CA. 'one's blown' means 'a thing that is blown'.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a mouth organ, an instrument played by blowing and drawing breath.

clue.text: Husband wearing tops or leather clothing

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the caps go round the H

parts.note: caps are tops, as on bottles or pens

explanation.surface: A husband chooses between tops or leather gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops' is caps, not shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaps are leather leggings worn over trousers by cowboys.

clue.text: Material obtained from dollar sign

parts.note: buck is informal for a dollar
the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Some fabric is obtained from, or bought with, a dollar sign: a money-themed scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' is a zodiac sign here, not the $ symbol the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiff cotton or linen cloth used in bookbinding and to stiffen clothes.

clue.text: A royal flag from the east African land

indicators.note: reading from the east in an across clue means right to left, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher
to flag is to tire or weaken

explanation.surface: A royal flag is flown from the east of some African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is a verb meaning weaken, not a banner; 'from the east' reads the whole run right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa, on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: Design pencilled in, an elementary machine

indicators.note: to design is to devise or form something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drawing of a simple machine has been pencilled in.
explanation.definitionFit: An inclined plane, a ramp, is one of the six classical simple machines of mechanics.

clue.text: French here penning in rebellious Brits

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: ici is French for here
en is French for in, the French of the clue applying to both words

explanation.surface: French-speaking guards hold rebellious Britons captive here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' governs both 'here' and 'in', giving ICI and EN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe who, under Boudicca, rose in revolt against Roman rule.

clue.text: Bad actor, trashed, promises to return ready

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters of the word are scrambled

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay back money, and 'ready' is slang for cash

explanation.surface: A poor actor got slated by critics and keeps vowing to make a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' means ready money, i.e. cash, so the IOUs are promises to repay.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means extremely bad or of very poor quality, an intensified synonym.

clue.text: Without notice, plans ambush in grand retinue

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: someone who plans an ambush lies in wait
an advertisement, or ad, is a notice
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Without warning, someone plots an ambush inside a grand royal entourage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside, so the ambush phrase wraps the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies-in-waiting are noblewomen attending a queen or princess, forming part of her retinue.

clue.text: Strong beast with three feet lifted junk

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a yard is three feet
both junk and horse are slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A strong animal with three feet hoisted up some junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns YARD to DRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray horse is a powerful breed for pulling heavy carts, a strong beast of burden.

clue.text: Communicate what wrong answer may do

definitions.meaning: to get something across is to communicate it
a wrong answer may ... from the marker

explanation.definitionFit: To get an idea across is to make others understand it; a marked error gets a cross.

clue.text: Prediction heard if warning players

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for if is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: whether is a synonym of if, as in 'ask if he's coming'
fore is the golfer's shout warning of a flying ball
the cast are the players in a show

explanation.surface: A prediction overheard, about whether a warning will reach the performers.
explanation.walkthrough: Only WHETHER is sounded out; FORE is a golfing cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecast is a prediction of the coming conditions in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Statesman Berliner once beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Berlin was capital of Prussia, so a Berliner was once a Prussian

explanation.surface: A statesman from Berlin was executed long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian is a man of the Russian state, a citizen, as this clue reads statesman.

clue.text: This person's given a subsidy, turning up Asian art

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: this person is I, the writer, so 'this person's' is I'M, I am
a giro is a British state benefit payment, once paid by giro cheque

explanation.surface: Someone receiving a grant turns up to study Asian art.
explanation.walkthrough: A giro was the British unemployment benefit cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of paper folding.

clue.text: Teacher back in classroom? I see teacher returning greeting

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: aha is an exclamation of sudden understanding, like 'I see'

indicators.note: returning means the word for teacher is read backwards

parts.note: sir is what pupils call a male teacher
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Back in a classroom, a pupil realises the teacher is turning round to greet the class.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Teacher' is the definition; 'back in' takes the last letter of classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharishi is a Hindu sage or spiritual guide, a guru who instructs disciples.

clue.text: Left-winger, but not a wet

indicators.note: but not means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a Maoist is a left-wing follower of Mao

explanation.surface: A left-winger, but not one of the weak moderates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' looks like a political insult for a moderate, but it is the definition meaning damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet or damp.

clue.text: Woke clutching auntie, oddly, in fear

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: woke attitudes are often called PC, politically correct

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone woke up clinging to an aunt, gripped by fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woke' is the adjective meaning PC, not 'woke up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear or alarm, a near synonym.

clue.text: Marsh is often seen by this tree

definitions.text: Marsh is often seen by this
definitions.meaning: ... Marsh was a New Zealand crime writer, so her first name sits beside Marsh

explanation.definitionFit: The ngaio is a small native New Zealand tree, and the author was named after it.

clue.text: National football team maintaining king's backing

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: a football team has eleven players, written here as 11, i.e. II

indicators.note: backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's king, so king's gives LEAR'S

explanation.surface: A national football team is keeping up support for its king.
explanation.walkthrough: The eleven is written as the digits 11, read as the letters II. 'king's' is King Lear's, from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a national, a citizen, of the state of Israel.

clue.text: Old Henry, a soldier, forced back Amerindian

indicators.note: forced back means the whole sequence is turned around

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
a para is a paratrooper

explanation.surface: An old Henry and a soldier are pushed back by a Native American warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' is the electrical unit H, not a king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a Native American people of the Great Plains, so a member is an Amerindian.

clue.text: Join head of retail bank

parts.note: to tie is to join or fasten

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to sign up with the boss of a retail bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a row or rank, not a financial institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of seats is a tier, one row raised above another.

clue.text: Native American trails outside of Edmonton in shade

indicators.note: trails means comes after, so this piece goes at the end
in places the outer letters inside the colour

parts.note: indigo is a deep blue shade

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Native American follows trails outside Edmonton, in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native American' looks like one phrase, but 'Native' alone is the definition; 'American' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigenous means belonging to a place originally, as a native does.
